records.title: GF180MCU Design Manual 14.1 — Chip operating conditions and thin/thick gate-oxide reliability limits
records.process: GF180MCU 3.3 V LV thin oxide and 5 V/6 V higher-voltage thick gate
records.architecture: Reliability depends on terminal-to-terminal stress, exposure time/duty and operating conditions; nominal supply class is not a universal terminal rating

data.label: Thin-oxide DC gate-to-other-node absolute limit
data.conditions: Section 14.1.4.2; applies between gate and any other FET node, not simply chip supply voltage.

data.label: Nominal voltage classes
data.conditions: Section 14.1.2: 3.3 V LV, 5/6 V HV; drain HCI and gate-oxide constraints must both be satisfied.

records.supports: 6 V vs 3.3 V is a voltage/gate-oxide device choice within silicon CMOS; startup and coupled-node overshoot need terminal stress review.
records.does_not_support: Do not treat a model solving at a voltage as proof of long-term reliability; 3.3 V thin-oxide devices cannot simply replace our 6 V output without a voltage-domain design.
records.notes: Public text lists a thick-gate DC value as 6.5V/6V for the 5V/6V process; avoid rearranging those into a universal 6.6 V gate rating. HCI and TDDB lifetime/duty constraints are separate. No unpublished material stack inferred.
